newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada ticket agents set strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada ticket agents set strike deadline.

text.p: The union representing Air Canada's 3,500 customer sales and service agents Wednesday set a Dec. 5 deadline for a strike at Canada's biggest airline.

The Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) said members of its local 2213 voted 91 percent for strike action to back contract demands. The main issues for the union are wages, benefits and job security, the CAW said.

Negotiations between the carrier and the CAW broke off on Sept. 28 after an unsuccessful attempt at resolving the impasse with the help of a federal government conciliator. Talks were set to resume on Dec. 2, the union said.
"I'm not sure a strike can be averted," said Cheryl Kryzaniwsky, president of local 2213.
The 3,500 union members work at airports, in the airline's Aeroplan travel miles programme and at reservations and ticket offices across Canada.
Air Canada is also in contract negotiations with about 3,300 flight attendants, who rejected an earlier contract offer.
Air Canada usually schedules most of its unionized worker contracts to end in the same year so that the airline is not perpetually negotiating with employees.
